title: European Commission — Digital Batteries Passport: data points by category
usedFor: The Commission's own data-point list for the battery passport, with per-category applicability and, per data point, the exact Annex/Article citation — the single most valuable gap-analysis input this register has produced.
licence: CC BY 4.0, confirmed 2026-08-11 directly from the document's own page 3: reuse authorised under Commission Decision 2011/833/EU, licensed CC BY 4.0, attribution required. No longer 'reported' — read verbatim.
source: https://single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu/document/download/cd1e5e6c-4a4a-4b99-995a-49eb6916187e_en — fetched directly from the Commission's own site, not the third-party mirror. "Guidance Document: Digital Batteries Passport – data points by category", Version 1.0, 28 July 2026, DG GROW Directorate G Unit G2. Electronically signed 03/08/2026. The download URL above is the citable source.
finding: Confirms the survey's prior IRI concern (Commission mints none) and resolves its metadata worry: 'v1.0 as of February 2027' was the survey's own conflation of the document's publish date (28 July 2026) with the *applicability* date it states inside (February 2027) — the primary document's own dating is internally consistent, nothing was actually wrong here once read directly. Covers EV, LMT and industrial batteries only (Art. 3 categories) — not portable or SLI. All 71 numbered data points read against `BatteryData` (`crates/dpp-domain/src/product_group/data/battery/data.rs`), each with its own Annex VI/XIII citation from the Commission itself. Confirmed matches: battery category, manufacturer identity (envelope-level), model ID, place/date of manufacture, weight, capacity, chemistry, critical raw materials, all four recycled-content percentages, expected lifetime in cycles, cathode/anode/electrolyte composition, and the entire Annex VII state-of-health parameter set (SOCE / remaining capacity / power capability / round-trip efficiency / self-discharge / ohmic resistance) — `StateOfHealth`'s two-variant design matches the Commission's own EV-vs-stationary/LMT split exactly. Gaps found here **triple-corroborate** the same gaps `batterypass-samm` and `catena-x-battery-pass` found independently, now each with the Commission's own citation: hazardous substances other than Hg/Cd/Pb (Annex VI A(8)) — nothing analogous to `SvhcSubstance`; usable extinguishing agent (Annex VI A(9)); share of renewable content (Annex XIII 1(f)) — distinct from recycled content, wholly absent; minimum and maximum voltage (Annex XIII 1(h)) — only nominal voltage is modelled; original power capability and power limits (Annex XIII 1(i)) — no power field exists at all; reference test used for expected lifetime (Annex XIII 1(j)); capacity threshold for exhaustion (Annex XIII 1(k)); commercial warranty period (Annex XIII 1(m)); C-rate of the cycle-life test (Annex XIII 1(p)); Art. 13(4)/13(5) marking requirements (Annex XIII 1(q)); EU declaration of conformity reference (Annex XIII 1(r)); waste-battery prevention/management info per Art. 74(1)(a)-(f) (Annex XIII 1(s)); part numbers and spare-parts sourcing contacts (Annex XIII 2(b)); safety measures (Annex XIII 2(d)); test-report results proving compliance (Annex XIII 3); capacity/power/round-trip-efficiency fade and internal-resistance increase, all four as dynamic (individual-battery, not model-level) figures (Annex XIII 4(a)); expected lifetime in calendar years, distinct from cycles (Annex XIII 4(a)); battery status — original/repurposed/re-used/remanufactured/waste (Annex XIII 4(c)); and periodic charge-cycle/state-of-charge/negative-event recording (Annex XIII 4(d)), of which `HarmfulEvents` only partially covers. Two items are correctly *not* gaps: the carbon footprint declaration/label (Annex XIII 1(c)) is explicitly 'not to be filled/displayed as of February 2027 — format still to be specified in the upcoming implementing act', matching our own correctly-blocked CFB stub; likewise the printable-instructions requirement (Annex XIII 1(t)) is on hold pending Omnibus IV. **Re-checked 2026-10-13, reading the same URL again:** it now serves Version 2.0, dated 15 August 2026 (manuscript completed August 2026), not Version 1.0 of 28 July 2026. The reuse statement is unchanged: Commission Decision 2011/833/EU, CC BY 4.0, credit required. The data points are still numbered to 71 and the document carries no change log, so what changed between 1.0 and 2.0 is not stated and was not worked out here. The field-by-field comparison and the 20 gaps above were made against 1.0 and have not been repeated against 2.0. The battery schema's 2.8.0 description says it follows version 2.0, so part of that comparison has since been made in the schema, but this record was not updated from it.
nextStep: This document supplies the citation every one of the 20 gaps above needs — no further primary-text search is required for most of them, only deciding field shape and schema version. Sequence by what the Commission marks Mandatory-now for the most categories first: hazardous substances, renewable content, min/max voltage, power, warranty period, C-rate, marking/conformity-declaration references, and waste-battery info are all Mandatory today for at least EV and LMT. The dynamic/individual-battery vs. static/model-level distinction (Annex XIII point 4 vs. points 1-3) is architectural, not a field list — `BatteryData` does not currently distinguish declared model-level figures from measured individual-battery ones the way `StateOfHealth`/`ExpectedLifetime` already do for state-of-health; the new fade/resistance-increase/cycle-count fields belong in that same disclosure-gated, per-battery shape, not as flat `BatteryData` additions. Repeat the comparison against Version 2.0 before acting on any gap listed above; the gap list is for 1.0.
